object_entity.event_label: Sardinian Exile of Hippolytus and Pontian
object_entity.notes: Bishop Pontian and the schismatic Hippolytus were both exiled to the mines of Sardinia in 235 under Emperor Maximinus Thrax; they were reconciled before death; their bodies were brought back to Rome by Pope Fabian c. 236.

context_place.notes: Imperial capital associated with the Roman church and Paul later ministry.

evidence.notes: HE 6.43: Cornelius's letter describes Fabian retrieving bodies of Pontian and Hippolytus from Sardinia, establishing his role in this event.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Eusebius preserves a letter of Cornelius of Rome describing Novatian's ordination irregularity: three simple and rustic bishops from Italy were brought to Rome and compelled to lay hands on Novatian by a counterfeit and vain laying on of hands; Novatian seized the bishopric by craft and treachery. Cornelius also lists the Roman clergy: forty-six presbyters, seven deacons, seven subdeacons, forty-two acolytes, and fifty-two exorcists, readers, and doorkeepers. More than fifteen hundred widows and distressed persons are supported by the Lord's grace and kindness.
passage.notes: Cornelius on Novatian's irregular ordination; Roman church size and clerical orders c. 251

object_entity.description: The Acts of Thomas (3rd c.) narrates Thomas's journey to India; the Thomas Christian tradition in Malabar claims apostolic origin; certainty is claimed_tradition.

evidence.notes: Passage contextualizes rufinus-of-aquileia's position on thomas-preached-in-india.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: A philosopher named Meropius of Tyre sailed to India with two boys Frumentius and Aedesius. The ship was seized and all killed except the boys who were brought to the king of Aksum. When the king died the queen asked Frumentius to help govern. Frumentius sought out Roman traders who were Christians and built churches. Later he traveled to Alexandria where Athanasius consecrated him bishop. He returned to Aksum and converted many including the king.
passage.notes: Primary Western source for the christianization of Aksum; Rufinus heard the account from Aedesius himself.
